sources.title: o3-deep-research model reference
sources.evidence: The exact model reference identifies alias o3-deep-research and default snapshot o3-deep-research-2025-06-26. It documents 200,000 context tokens, text/image input, text output, reasoning, prompt caching and hosted research tools. The current Markdown reference marks both model and snapshot Shut down. It supplies no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Introducing deep research
sources.evidence: The contemporaneous page is dated February 2, 2025 and launches deep research in ChatGPT for Pro users. It describes an early/upcoming o3 variant trained for browsing and data analysis, including Python. Later updates and the lightweight o4-mini version are distinct from this original release. Read through the indexed primary page; a separate direct HTTP fetch returned 403.

sources.title: Deep research in the API, webhooks, and web search with o3
sources.evidence: The June 26, 2025 announcement explicitly identifies o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research as the same deep research models already available in ChatGPT, now offered in the API. Read the original first post through the topic JSON; its author is Nikunj Handa and the metadata identifies OpenAI Staff and administrator. This binds the research-model lineage, without proving byte-identical February and June checkpoints.

sources.title: Deep Research System Card, February 25, 2025
sources.evidence: The complete PDF describes an early o3 variant trained with reinforcement learning on research browsing tasks and Python use. Section 3.2 separately identifies an o3-mini model that summarizes the research model’s chain of thought. Training and evaluation sections disclose neither total/active parameters nor detailed network topology. Research-model counts must not include or borrow the summarizer’s size.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: The June 2025 section places the release of o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research under June 24, while listing June 26 snapshot identifiers. This conflicts with the June 26 contemporaneous API announcement, so the snapshot suffix alone cannot settle the API launch day. Both are later than the original ChatGPT research-model release.

sources.title: Deep research API guide
sources.evidence: The reference describes web search, file search, specialized MCP search/fetch servers and code interpreter support for the exact model. It explicitly excludes other tools such as custom function calling. Its introductory retirement notice retains examples for reference after July 23, 2026; these examples are not evidence of current endpoint operation.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 notice states that access to o3-deep-research and o3-deep-research-2025-06-26 shut down on July 23, 2026. The replacement listed is gpt-5.6-sol. This exact alias/snapshot notice controls over an older indexed model-page Deprecated label.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: This archived engineering recipe expressly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Section 2.1 explains that prompt caching reuses key/value projections in Transformer attention layers. Combined with the exact o3-deep-research reference’s explicit prompt-caching support, this supports a qualified broad Transformer inference, not a dense/MoE topology or parameter count.

sources.title: ChatGPT Agent System Card, July 17, 2025
sources.evidence: The complete later report’s Table 6 has an explicit Deep research comparison column with multilingual evaluation results. It does not disclose parameter counts or architecture for that research model. Its new ChatGPT agent is a different model in the o3 family; its tool combination does not redefine this API variant.

sources.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card, April 16, 2025
sources.evidence: The later report describes general o3/o4-mini reasoning and training and refers back to deep research’s safety evaluations. Reviewed the complete PDF and model comparison tables: it supplies no exact o3-deep-research total/active count or detailed topology. Base o3 and o4-mini columns are not research-variant specifications.

sources.title: OpenAI GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Reviewed the full OpenAI-authored report linked by the official GPT-5 system-card page, including its training section and model progression/comparison tables. The version retrieved was revised May 1, 2026. It names base o3 and o3 Pro, not an exact o3-deep-research parameter column, and provides no parameter or topology disclosure for this research variant.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The agreement governs hosted API service access, grants access/use rights and retains OpenAI intellectual-property rights. Together with the exact hosted model reference and launch, this supports the descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license. Read the indexed primary text; direct HTTP fetch returned 403.

sources.title: File inputs API guide
sources.evidence: The guide explains that PDF input is parsed into extracted text and page images for vision-capable models. File processing is distinct from a native PDF encoder or image generation. No audio/video input or image output is established for the exact research model.

sources.title: Introduction to the Deep Research API
sources.evidence: The archived recipe names o3-deep-research-2025-06-26 and distinguishes it from the lighter o4-mini-deep-research snapshot. Its code demonstrates Responses API web search, reasoning summaries and optional code interpreter. The recipe is historical and does not establish current availability.

sources.title: Models.dev upstream record
sources.evidence: The inspected upstream lead labels the family o, uses June 26, 2025 as the API release and gives 200,000 context, image/text input and reasoning/tools. Its catalog claims were checked against the primary sources above; it is not the basis for the revised earliest release or architecture.

name.note: Exact research-model alias; the API reference binds it to o3-deep-research-2025-06-26. It is distinct from base o3, o3-pro and o4-mini-deep-research.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes the model reference, original announcement and research-system card.

family.note: Use the documented o3 lineage instead of the broad o-series prefix. The original research variant used an early o3 model; the separate o3-mini summarizer is not the model being indexed.

release_date.note: Earliest public availability of the o3 research variant was the February 2 ChatGPT launch. The later official API announcement explicitly binds o3-deep-research to that ChatGPT research offering. This is a product-lineage date, not a claim that the June 26 API checkpoint existed in February. The current changelog says June 24 for API release while the contemporaneous API announcement is June 26; preserve that conflict separately.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is a hosted OpenAI service; the accessed primary release and model reference provide no downloadable checkpoint or open-weight grant.

license.note: Descriptive licensing classification for hosted API access under OpenAI terms. This is not an open-source model-weight license or a claim that service outputs are owned by OpenAI.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count for this exact research variant was found in its model reference, original training/system card, or the later ChatGPT Agent, o3/o4-mini and GPT-5 reports checked. The later Deep research comparison column reports benchmark performance, not size. Do not borrow base-o3 or summarizer values.

active_parameters_b.note: The primary material checked provides no active parameter count or activation definition for this variant. No dense/MoE topology is disclosed, so neither equality with an unknown total nor a routed active count is justified.

architecture.note: Qualified architectural inference: this exact model explicitly supports prompt caching, and OpenAI’s applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering recipe describes that mechanism as caching Transformer attention key/value projections. This supports only the broad Transformer label. Exact variant training/interpretability searches and the accessed reports did not establish dense/MoE structure, layer counts, expert routing or the complete multimodal topology.

context_window.note: Last documented API context in tokens for the alias/default June 26 snapshot, distinct from the separately listed 100,000-token output cap. This value is not asserted for the original February ChatGPT deployment. The API model shut down on July 23, 2026.

modalities.note: The exact API model reference documents text/image input and file uploads. The API file-input guide documents PDF support for vision-capable models through extracted text and page images. Include pdf as a supported input format, not as a native PDF encoder. Python plots or embedded web images are tool artifacts, not native image output. No audio/video capability is established.

reasoning.note: The exact API reference documents reasoning-token support. The original card describes reinforcement learning for multi-step research reasoning; this is distinct from the separate o3-mini summarizer used in ChatGPT.

tool_call.note: True for documented web search, file search, code interpreter and constrained MCP search/fetch calls. Custom function calling and arbitrary MCP interfaces are explicitly unsupported. These are last documented capabilities, not a claim that the retired endpoint accepts requests.

description.value: OpenAI o3 variant trained for multi-step web research and data analysis, with text and image input and cited text reports.
description.note: Plain description of the research specialization and documented modalities; avoids the model reference’s unsupported comparative superlatives. Retirement and API/date scope belong in the notes.

patch.notes: The release date is the February 2, 2025 ChatGPT debut of the o3 research variant. OpenAI’s later API announcement identifies o3-deep-research as the same ChatGPT research offering. The June 26 API snapshot is a later identifier; checkpoint identity across those dates is not established. The current API changelog lists June 24, while the contemporaneous API announcement is dated June 26. The 200,000-token context and text/image input specifications describe the last documented API snapshot, o3-deep-research-2025-06-26, not necessarily the original ChatGPT deployment. OpenAI shut down the alias and dated API snapshot on July 23, 2026. Tool support covers web search, file search, code interpreter and MCP search/fetch. Custom function calling and arbitrary MCP tool interfaces are unsupported. PDF processing and Python-generated figures are service/tool capabilities, not additional native modalities. Transformer is a broad inference from exact-model prompt-caching support and OpenAI’s applicable engineering explanation. Dense/MoE structure and total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked primary sources. The separate o3-mini chain-of-thought summarizer is excluded from this model’s specifications.

summary: Corrected family to o3 and earliest release to February 2, 2025 using the original ChatGPT announcement and explicit later API identity bridge. Recorded the June 24/June 26 API-date conflict, historical snapshot scope and July 23, 2026 shutdown. Added Proprietary licensing and a qualified Transformer inference; total/active counts remain undisclosed after original and later exact-model comparison checks. Confirmed historical 200K context, text/image input plus qualified PDF file input, reasoning and constrained research-tool calls, with custom functions explicitly unsupported. Replaced the generic description.
